title: Split metering paths for speculative prefetch vs executed toolcalls on non-chat endpoints
creator: Aisha Park
description: Context: We currently conflate speculative prefetch requests (e.g., prefetching embeddings/rerank vectors or speculative tool invocation candidates) with executed toolcall/structured-output billing in the same metering path. This causes overcharging in scenarios where prefetches are abandoned, partially executed, or retried across retries and fanout stages. Goal: introduce a separated metering model that treats speculative prefetches as provisional credits (logged but not finalized) and finalizes billing only for executed toolcalls and structured outputs, with clear refund/proration rules for cancelled or partially-successful flows. This ticket covers the runtime changes, accounting ledger updates, API surface adjustments, and migration path for historical attribution.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Prefetch requests are recorded to a provisional ledger with unique prefetch_id and do not increment user billable counters until finalized. 2) When a prefetch results in an executed toolcall/structured output, the billing system atomically moves the charge from provisional to final with stable provenance (request_id -> prefetch_id -> execution_id). 3) Abandoned or expired prefetches are reconciled nightly and either auto-refunded or credited per policy; no customer sees unreconciled provisional charges on invoices. 4) Partial execution (e.g., 2 of 4 fanout items execute) results in correct per-item billing with deterministic proration and a clear audit trail. 5) Rollout can be toggled via feature-flag per-cluster and has an automatic rollback on discrepancy >0.5% vs control group for 24h. 6) Metric dashboards (billing.delta_prefetch_vs_final, billing.refunds_daily) are present and validated against golden data for the first 7 days.
design_summary: Proposed approach: (a) Add a lightweight provisional ledger table that stores prefetch_id, request_id, model_variant, tokens_estimate, kv_prefetch_digest, timestamp, and status (pending/finalized/cancelled). (b) Require prefetch flows to include idempotency tokens and attach prefetch_id to any downstream execution requests. (c) Modify the accounting pipeline: prefetch writes provisional entries; execution path performs an atomic upsert that marks provisional entries as finalized and emits a finalize-event to billing stream. (d) For prefetch-only flows (never executed), run daily reconciliation that emits refund/credit operations if prefetches exceed retention window. (e) Introduce a 'billing_mode' enum for endpoints: prefetched, immediate, and batched; default for embeddings/rerank speculative fanout becomes prefetched. Trade-offs: adding provisional ledger increases write amplification for high fanout workloads; mitigated by compacting prefetch metadata (digest) and rate-limiting prefetches per API key. See design doc: https://confluence.redwood/inference/billing/prefetch-metering-v2
rollout_plan: 1) Merge feature-flagged runtime changes behind FF:metering.prefetch_v2. 2) Start with internal traffic and 1% customer sample (day 1) comparing new finalization events vs legacy accounting. 3) Validate metrics for 48h, then increase to 10% for 5 days. 4) Enable for all hosted read-only traffic (no billing) and run reconciliation sim for another 48h. 5) Open beta for non-sensitive customers (opt-in) for 7 days. 6) Full enable with nightly reconciliation for 14 days and hold. 7) Complete migration: retroactively reconcile last 7 days of provisional entries to ensure no invoice drift. Rollback plan: if billing divergence >0.5% or failed reconciliations >0.1% of prefetches, disable FF and initiate incident runbook (billing-incident-02).
test_plan: Unit tests for provisional ledger writes and finalize atomicity; integration tests that simulate fanout 1..8 prefetches with random cancellations and partial failures; property tests for idempotency across retries; load-test the provisional ledger with synthetic traffic matching 95th percentile fanout; end-to-end validation using a golden dataset (billing-golden/prefetch_v2) where expected credits/refunds are asserted; canary dashboards: billing.delta_prefetch_vs_final, raw.prefetch_rate, reconciliation.failures, invoice_drift_pct. Include a smoke test that queries invoices API to verify no provisional entries leak into invoice line items.
